title: Admin-console reads zeroTrustGate at apply-time and switches sign-in surface (recommendedDefault true)
context: application-admin-console v1.0.0 shipped with principalDirectory as the sole hard requirement; sign-in surface was local per whatever security-auth-* was applied. Round-6 T-4 introduces edge-cloudflare-access with the zeroTrustGate capability; a composed deployment needs the admin-console to flip its sign-in surface deterministically.
decision: application-admin-console v1.1.0 reads appliedCapabilities via readAppliedCapabilities at apply-time. When zeroTrustGate is present the sign-in surface renders access-gated (no local form, principal reads from request.auth); when absent the surface falls back to whatever security-auth-* is applied. Q4 default (spec 5.4.1): zeroTrustGate is CONSUMED OPTIONALLY; principalDirectory remains the sole hard requirement (making Access-gate hard is a v2.0 change). Standards trace clause: visual round spec section 5.5.2 (the T-5 mechanism). recommendedDefault: true.
consequences: The v1.1.0 admin-console remains backward-compatible with every v1.0.0 deployment. An Access-gated deployment automatically stops rendering the local login form; the local-login surface still ships in v1.1.0 (fallback branch when zeroTrustGate absent).
